checks_performed.no_implementation_code_present: FAIL. Section 3.1 and section 3.2 each contain a full `defmodule Letflow.Simulation.Scenario do ... defstruct [...] end` / `defmodule Letflow.Simulation.RunReport do ... defstruct [...] end` block -- complete, syntactically valid Elixir module definitions with nested @type declarations and defstruct field-default lists, not bare @spec-style signatures. This is materially different from how the OTHER design this session that reached PASS with an equivalent struct/type-shape need (lib/letflow/design/req203-artifact-activation.md, §2.1-2.3 for its three new schemas, §4.1 for its Ecto.Multi-returning function) expressed the identical kind of information: req203 uses prose/markdown tables (column | type | constraints) for every schema shape and single-line inline type signatures for functions (e.g. `Letflow.Repository.Activation.resolve(artifact_kind :: artifact_kind(), ...) :: {:ok, ArtifactVersion.t()} | {:error, :not_activated} | ...`), with zero `defmodule`/`defstruct` code fences anywhere in the document. REQ-157's own rework history (commits 3680243/f9b3a0b/b88e051) establishes this session's working standard precisely: '@spec/@type blocks are permitted' but a design must not present something 'copy-paste-ready' as if it were real source -- and a full `defmodule ... defstruct [...] end` block IS copy-paste-ready: it could be pasted verbatim into test/support/simulation/scenario.ex and would compile and run as the real module, unlike a bare @type or @spec line, which cannot stand alone as a working module. Per this role's mandate ('FAIL immediately and completely on any single failed check -- no partial credit'; 'no partial credit' for being 'otherwise strong'), sections 3.1 and 3.2 must be rewritten as prose/table field descriptions (field name | type | description, matching req203's §2.1-2.3 convention) with no defmodule/defstruct wrapper, before this design can pass.
checks_performed.open_questions_oq1_oq4: OQ-2 FAILS the 'not silently resolved when resolvable now' standard this session already applied to REQ-202/REQ-203's validators. §2.3 already states the design read `list_groups/1`'s @spec at lib/letflow/identity.ex:527, but the design had (and used) read access to that function's full BODY too -- independently re-read here: `def list_groups(opts)` (lib/letflow/identity.ex lines 527-537) takes only `opts :: opts()` (a `prefix:` keyword list), builds `from(g in Group, order_by: [asc: g.name])` with NO name/filter clause of any kind, and returns the full unpaginated per-tenant list. There is no server-side name filter to discover -- this is a settled fact, not an open question. §2.3 must be corrected to state plainly: `list_groups/1` accepts no name filter; `seed_groups/2`'s idempotency pre-check must list the tenant's groups via `list_groups/1` and match the fixture's group name client-side, full stop -- not phrased as 'if no by-name lookup exists... resolved by ELIXIR-DEV against list_groups/1's actual filter parameters,' which defers a question this design's own §0 already had the material to answer. OQ-1, OQ-3, OQ-4 remain legitimate: OQ-1 (Tenant.t()'s exact prefix-field name) and OQ-4 (yaml_elixir's YAML 1.1 scalar-coercion fidelity against not-yet-ported fixture content) both require information the design could not have resolved from this session's read set alone (OQ-1 needs lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex, not in artifacts_in; OQ-4 needs the actual fixture content, not yet ported); OQ-3 is correctly scoped out since REQ-206/207/208's scenario content does not exist yet in this requirement's scope.
